title: Menelik Palace
scope: Publicly interpretable historic exteriors of the Great Ghebbi in Addis Ababa: Menelik II’s royal residence, Throne House, Banquet Hall and Baeta Maryam mausoleum.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: Visitor authority identifies the surviving throne and banquet halls in the public heritage park.
ETH Library states PDM items can be reused without restriction.
Explains that Swiss copyright was not restored for Walter Mittelholzer before application of URAA.

limitations: Meshes cover four historic exteriors only. The balance of the palace compound, additions, grounds and interiors are outside scope.
The archive photos control the four massings and the mausoleum’s arcades, drum and domes. Roof sections, window placement and later restoration finishes of the residence and halls are estimates.
Footprints and headings come from current map outlines. Original Terrarium sampling controls the sloped site; precise threshold heights are estimates.
next: Author the palace residence, throne and banquet halls and the domed mausoleum.
